mainTopic: How we know that a זר, and an אונן, ruin the עבודה: logical proofs and sources from פסוקים
overview: The גמרא wants to prove that a זר who does the sacrificial service ruins it (חילל). It first tries a קל וחומר from a בעל מום. When that is knocked down, it builds a הצד השוה from a בעל מום and a טמא, and then from a בעל מום and an אונן. Each time it answers attacks along the way, including one about serving on a במה, which רב סמא pushes back on. רב משרשיא offers a different proof, a קל וחומר from a כהן who served sitting. The גמרא defends it, and also shows from 'לפני ה׳' that a sitting כהן is fit on a במה. Then the גמרא turns to the אונן and brings two פסוקים as sources: one from the כהן גדול who does not leave the מקדש, and רבי אלעזר's from אהרן's answer 'הן הקריבו'. It explains why each side does not use the other's פסוק. The amud ends as the school of רבי ישמעאל begins a קל וחומר from a בעל מום, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the logical argument from a blemished priest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes its קל וחומר: if a בעל מום, who may eat קדשי קדשים, ruins the service when he does it, then a זר, who may not even eat, should surely ruin it too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then a non-priest, who is not allowed to eat the holy meat, isn't it obvious that if he did the service he ruined it?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a logical proof that a זר who does the service ruins it. This sentence completes the argument that began just before, with the case of a בעל מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, the גמרא said: a בעל מום is allowed to eat קדשי קדשים, yet if he serves he ruins the עבודה. A זר is weaker, since he is not even allowed to eat. So it seems obvious that a זר who serves ruins the עבודה even more.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-כהן, someone who is not from the priestly family
Isn't it logical? The phrase that finishes a קל וחומר
He performed the sacrificial service
He desecrated, meaning he made the service invalid

phrases.english: A non-priest, who does not eat,
phrases.notes: He means he may not eat the meat of קדשי קדשים, which even a blemished כהן may eat.

phrases.english: is it not logical that if he served, he desecrated the service?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the קל וחומר from בעל מום that began just before this text.
steps.raayaObject: That a זר who performs עבודה makes it invalid
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from a בעל מום, who may eat yet still invalidates the service

steps.title: The blemished priest has a special strictness
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר is rejected: a בעל מום is special, because the Torah treats a blemished כהן just like a blemished animal. Both are unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a blemished priest? He is special, because the Torah made the animal being offered like the one offering it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from step 1. It points out something stricter about a בעל מום that a זר does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemish disqualifies both the animal and the כהן, so the Torah treats them the same way. That gives the בעל מום an extra strictness. Maybe that strictness is why he ruins the service, and a זר, who lacks it, would not.

keyTerms.meaning: What about...? The opening of a פִּירְכָא, a reason the two cases are not really alike
A כהן with a physical blemish
The thing that is offered, meaning the animal
The one who offers it, meaning the כהן

phrases.english: What about a blemished priest?
He is special, since with him the Torah made the offering like the one who offers it!
phrases.notes: A blemish makes both the animal and the כהן unfit, so here they are treated the same.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְבַעַל מוּם שֶׁכֵּן עָשָׂה בּוֹ קָרֵב כְּמַקְרִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the קל וחומר of step 1 with a פירכא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole קל וחומר from בעל מום
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A בעל מום has an extra strictness, since he is treated like a blemished animal, and a זר does not have that strictness

steps.title: The impure priest shows the strictness doesn't matter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends the proof by pointing to a טמא כהן. He does not have the 'like the animal' strictness, yet he still ruins the service.
steps.simpleTranslation: An impure priest will prove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection of step 2 by bringing a different case, a טמא. It says this case proves the objection does not hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With טומאה, the animal and the כהן are not treated the same way, yet a טמא כהן still ruins the service. So ruining the service is not caused by the 'like the animal' strictness. The proof can be rebuilt using the טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: A ritually impure כהן
Will prove, meaning this case shows the objection is wrong

phrases.english: An impure priest will prove it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פירכא of step 2 by showing a case without that strictness that still invalidates.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-example that removes the force of the פירכא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'like the animal' strictness is what makes a בעל מום ruin the service
steps.terutzMaskana: A טמא lacks that strictness yet ruins the service, so the strictness is not the reason

steps.title: The impure priest has his own strictness
steps.stepSummary: The proof from a טמא is rejected: a טמא is special because he spreads impurity to others, and a זר does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about an impure priest? He is special, because he makes others impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from the טמא. It finds a different strictness that only a טמא has.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טמא can pass his impurity on to people and things. That is a serious strictness a זר does not have. So maybe that is why the טמא ruins the service.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes others impure

phrases.english: What about an impure priest?
He is special, since he makes others impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the counter-proof of step 3 with a new פירכא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Learning a זר from a טמא alone
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A טמא spreads impurity, a strictness that a זר lacks

steps.title: The blemished priest shows that strictness doesn't matter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a בעל מום does not spread his blemish to anyone, yet he still ruins the service.
steps.simpleTranslation: A blemished priest will prove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection of step 4 by going back to the בעל מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemish cannot be passed to others, yet a בעל מום still ruins the service. So spreading impurity is not the real reason someone ruins the service.

phrases.english: A blemished priest will prove it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פירכא of step 4 by pointing back to the case refuted in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-example that removes the force of the פירכא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Spreading impurity is what makes a טמא ruin the service
steps.terutzMaskana: A בעל מום does not spread anything yet still ruins the service

steps.title: Combining both cases: what they share applies to a non-priest
steps.stepSummary: Each case has its own strictness, but what they share is that both are forbidden to serve and both ruin the service. A זר shares that, so he also ruins the service.
steps.simpleTranslation: The argument has gone around in a circle. This case is not like that one, and that one is not like this one. What they have in common is that they are forbidden to serve, and if they served they ruined it. So I will include a non-priest too: he is forbidden to serve, so if he served he ruined it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sees that each case has a weakness the other one covers. So it builds a הצד השוה argument from the two cases together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בעל מום's special strictness, being like the animal, is missing in the טמא. The טמא's special strictness, spreading impurity, is missing in the בעל מום. So neither special strictness can be the reason. The shared reason is that both are forbidden to serve, and a זר is forbidden too.

keyTerms.meaning: The argument has come back around, so each case answers the other's weakness
This case is not like that case, since each has its own unique feature
The common factor, the feature both cases share
They are warned, meaning forbidden by the Torah, from serving

steps.whatToRemember: A הצד השוה works when each source case has its own strictness that the other lacks. Then the only reason left is what they share. Here both a בעל מום and a טמא are forbidden to serve and ruin the service, so the same applies to a זר.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא threw out the בעל מום and the טמא because each was refuted. It is now using both together, and their combination is what makes the proof work.

phrases.english: And the argument has come back around.
The feature of this one is not like the feature of that one,
and the feature of that one is not like the feature of this one;
what they have in common is that they are forbidden to serve,
and if they served, they desecrated the service;
so I too will include a non-priest,
who is forbidden to serve, so if he served, he desecrated it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחָזַר הַדִּין לֹא רְאִי זֶה כִּרְאִי זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the two refuted cases from steps 2 to 5 into one הצד השוה proof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Through a הצד השוה from בעל מום and טמא, a זר who performs עבודה makes the service invalid.

steps.title: How do we know a non-priest is forbidden to serve?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a זר is forbidden to do the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that a non-priest is warned not to serve?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to check a key piece of the earlier proof. It asks where we learn that a זר is forbidden to serve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in step 6 said a זר is like a בעל מום and a טמא because all of them are forbidden to serve. That only works if we have a source that a זר really is forbidden. So the גמרא now looks for that source.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
Warned, forbidden by a Torah prohibition
A non-כהן

phrases.english: From where do we know that he is warned?
phrases.notes: "He" is the זר, the non-priest from the earlier proof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Checks a premise of the conclusion in step 6, namely that a זר is מוזהר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that forbids a זר from doing the עבודה.

steps.title: The source is 'a non-priest shall not come near you'
steps.stepSummary: The source cannot be ויינזרו, because that פסוק already mentions חילול. So the source must be וזר לא יקרב אליכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you learn it from 'they shall separate themselves', that פסוק already writes 'profaning' in it, so the proof would not be needed. Rather, you learn it from 'and a non-priest shall not come near you'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests one possible source and rejects it. Then it settles on a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the warning came from ויינזרו, the same פסוק already says ולא יחללו (profaning). Then the whole הצד השוה proof would be pointless, because the פסוק would say it outright. So the warning must come from וזר לא יקרב, which forbids a זר but does not mention ruining the service.

keyTerms.meaning: "They shall separate themselves" (ויקרא 22:2)
Profaning, making the service invalid
"A non-priest shall not come near you" (במדבר 18:4)

phrases.english: If from "that they separate themselves" –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:2

phrases.english: profaning itself is written in it!
phrases.notes: That same פסוק goes on to say "and they shall not profane", so we would not need the proof at all.

phrases.english: Rather, from "and a non-priest shall not come near you" –
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:4

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִוְּיִנָּזְרוּ חִילּוּל בְּגוּפֵיהּ כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ אֶלָּא מִוְּזָר לֹא יִקְרַב אֲלֵיכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The warning comes from וזר לא יקרב אליכם, a פסוק that forbids a זר but says nothing about חילול. That is why the הצד השוה proof is still needed.

steps.title: Blemished and impure priests were also banned from a private altar
steps.stepSummary: The shared feature of בעל מום and טמא can be broken down: both were forbidden even at a במה, but a זר was allowed there.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a way to break this down: what is special about the shared feature of the two cases? They were not allowed to serve on a private altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the הצד השוה proof again. The בעל מום and the טמא share a strictness that a זר does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When private altars (במה) were allowed, a non-priest could bring offerings on them. A בעל מום and a טמא could not. Maybe that extra strictness is the reason they ruin the service, and a זר, who was allowed at a במה, does not.

keyTerms.meaning: One can break this down, refute it
The shared feature of two cases
A private altar, allowed at certain times in history

phrases.english: There is room to refute:
what about the common element between them,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the בעל מום and the טמא from steps 2–6.

phrases.english: that they were not permitted on a private altar!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ מָה לְהַצַּד הַשָּׁוֶה שֶׁבָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the source for the warning on a זר now in place, the גמרא attacks the conclusion of step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole הצד השוה built from בעל מום and טמא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both sources were banned even at a במה. A זר was not, so the shared feature may carry a strictness that a זר lacks.

steps.title: Use a mourner instead of an impure priest
steps.stepSummary: Instead of the טמא, use an אונן, who was allowed at a במה, yet still ruins the service.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't say the impure priest proves it. Rather, say the mourner proves it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא swaps out the טמא and brings in a different case, an אונן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes here that an אונן was allowed to serve at a במה, so the attack of step 9 would not touch him. Yet in the מקדש he is forbidden to serve and ruins the service. So the במה point would not be what makes someone ruin the service.

keyTerms.meaning: A mourner on the day a close relative died
Will prove it
Don't say… rather say

phrases.english: Do not say: an impure one will prove it,
rather say: a mourner will prove it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא טָמֵא יוֹכִיחַ אֶלָּא אֵימָא אוֹנֵן יוֹכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 by replacing the טמא with an אונן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces one source case with another that avoids the objection.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only people banned even at a במה ruin the service, so a זר might not.
steps.terutzMaskana: An אונן was allowed at a במה and still ruins the service, so the במה point does not matter.

steps.title: A mourner is forbidden to eat second tithe
steps.stepSummary: The אונן has his own strictness: he may not eat מעשר שני, while a זר may.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about a mourner? He is forbidden to eat מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new case. An אונן has a strictness that a זר does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אונן may not eat מעשר שני, but a זר may eat it. So maybe an אונן ruins the service because of his extra strictness, and a זר still does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, מעשר שני, the second tithe eaten in ירושלים
Forbidden

phrases.english: What about a mourner –
that he is forbidden in tithe!
phrases.notes: He means an אונן may not eat מעשר שני.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the אונן brought in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Using the אונן as a source case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An אונן is forbidden to eat מעשר and a זר is not, so the אונן is stricter.

steps.title: A blemished priest proves it
steps.stepSummary: A בעל מום may eat מעשר, yet he still ruins the service.
steps.simpleTranslation: A blemished priest proves it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the attack on the אונן by pointing back to the בעל מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בעל מום is allowed to eat מעשר, yet he still ruins the service. So the מעשר rule is not what makes someone ruin the service.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן with a physical blemish

phrases.english: [A blemished one] will prove it.
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording; some versions read this line differently.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to another case that lacks the strictness raised in the objection.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only people forbidden in מעשר ruin the service.
steps.terutzMaskana: A בעל מום may eat מעשר and still ruins the service.

steps.title: The argument goes back around: a non-priest ruins the service
steps.stepSummary: The בעל מום and the אונן each have their own strictness. What they share is that both are forbidden to serve and both ruin the service, and a זר shares that.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the argument goes back around. This case is not like that case. Their shared feature is that they are forbidden to serve, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the back-and-forth. Using the בעל מום and the אונן, the הצד השוה proof stands, and a זר ruins the service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בעל מום has his own strictness, being treated like a blemished animal (step 2). The אונן has the מעשר strictness (step 11). Neither strictness is found in both, so neither can explain the shared rule. What both share is being forbidden to serve, and a זר is forbidden too, from וזר לא יקרב.

keyTerms.meaning: The argument goes back around to its starting point
This case is not like that case
Ruins, invalidates the service

steps.whatToRemember: A זר is forbidden to serve because of וזר לא יקרב. Through a הצד השוה from a בעל מום and an אונן, we learn that if he does serve, he ruins the service.
steps.confusionAlert: The final pair is not the same as the first pair. The טמא has been replaced by the אונן, but the shared feature, forbidden to serve and ruins the service, stays the same.

phrases.english: And the argument has gone back around,
the aspect of this is not like the aspect of that,
phrases.notes: "This" and "that" are now the בעל מום and the אונן.

phrases.english: their common element is that they are warned, etc.
phrases.notes: "Etc." means finish the line from step 6: they are forbidden, they ruin the service, and so a זר does too.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחָזַר הַדִּין לֹא רְאִי זֶה כִּרְאִי זֶה הַצַּד הַשָּׁוֶה שֶׁבָּהֶן שֶׁמּוּזְהָרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the cycle of steps 9–12 by rebuilding the הצד השוה from בעל מום and אונן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Since both a בעל מום and an אונן are forbidden to serve and ruin the service, a זר, who is forbidden by וזר לא יקרב, also ruins the service.

steps.title: Challenging the common element: neither was allowed at a במה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the shared feature of בעל מום and אונן can also be broken down, because neither was permitted to serve at a במה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, let us refute it: what is special about what they share? That they were not permitted at a private altar!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to knock down the conclusion from step 13 by finding a strictness that both the בעל מום and the אונן share, but a זר does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 said the בעל מום and the אונן share only one thing: both are forbidden to serve and both ruin the service. Now the גמרא proposes they share something more. Neither was allowed to serve at a במה, while a זר was. If so, the זר cannot be learned from them.

keyTerms.meaning: To refute or break down a derivation
The common element shared by two cases
A private altar, used in periods when it was permitted
They were permitted

phrases.english: Here too, let one refute:
What about their common element?
phrases.notes: "Their" means the בעל מום and the אונן from the last step.

phrases.english: That they were not permitted at a private altar!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion of step 13 using the same type of refutation as step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: The מה הצד derivation from בעל מום and אונן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both sources share a strictness, not being allowed at a במה, which a זר lacks, so the זר cannot be learned from them

steps.title: רב סמא: who says the אונן was forbidden at a במה?
steps.stepSummary: רב סמא בריה דרבא rejects the challenge. Nothing proves an אונן was forbidden at a במה, and perhaps he was permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב סמא son of רבא objected: who tells us an אונן was forbidden at a private altar? Maybe he was permitted there!
steps.whatsHappening: רב סמא pushes back against the challenge of step 14. He says we have no source that an אונן was forbidden at a במה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge only works if the אונן, like the בעל מום, was barred from the במה. רב סמא points out this is just an assumption. If an אונן was actually allowed at a במה, the two cases do not share that strictness, and the challenge falls.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to it (attacked the previous statement)
An acute mourner, on the day a close relative died
Perhaps
Permitted

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב סַמָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Samma son of Rava objects to it:
And who will tell us
that an acute mourner was forbidden at a private altar?
Perhaps he was permitted at a private altar!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב סַמָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation of step 14
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The factual assumption behind step 14's challenge
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is no source that an אונן was forbidden at a במה

steps.title: רב משרשיא: a קל וחומר from a כהן who served sitting
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא offers a different source. A sitting כהן may eat קדשים, yet he ruins the service. A זר may not eat, so surely he ruins it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: we learn it with a קל וחומר from a כהן who served sitting. That כהן eats קדשים, and still, if he served, he ruined it. A זר does not eat, so surely if he served he ruined it!
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא brings a completely new way to prove that a זר who serves ruins the עבודה. He uses a קל וחומר from a כהן who served while sitting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן who serves sitting is still a full כהן who may eat קדשים, yet his service is ruined (חילל). A זר is weaker, since he may not even eat קדשי קדשים. So if the stronger person ruins the service, the weaker person surely does.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stricter one
A כהן who served while sitting
He desecrated, meaning he ruined the service
A non-כהן

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya said:
It comes by an a fortiori argument from a sitting priest:
Just as a sitting priest, who eats [sacrificial meat],
if he served, he desecrated [the service];
a non-priest, who does not eat,
is it not logical that if he served, he desecrated?!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא אָמַר, אָתְיָא קַל וָחוֹמֶר מִיּוֹשֵׁב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new source after the במה discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זר who serves ruins the service, learned by קל וחומר from a כהן who served sitting

steps.title: A sitting person cannot testify
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר is challenged. A sitting person has a strictness of his own: he is disqualified from testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about a sitting person? He is disqualified from giving testimony!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב משרשיא's קל וחומר by finding something strict about יושב that does not apply to a זר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the source case is truly the lighter one. Sitting has a strictness of its own: a witness must stand, so a sitting person cannot testify. Because of that extra strictness, maybe that is why sitting ruins the service, and it tells us nothing about a זר.

keyTerms.meaning: Disqualified from giving testimony

phrases.english: What about a sitting person?
That he is disqualified from testimony!
phrases.notes: Witnesses have to stand while testifying, so sitting disqualifies them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the קל וחומר of step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: רב משרשיא's קל וחומר from יושב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יושב has an extra strictness (פסול לעדות) that a זר lacks, so the קל וחומר breaks

steps.title: Learn from a sitting תלמיד חכם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by learning from a sitting תלמיד חכם, who is not disqualified from testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn it from a תלמיד חכם who is sitting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the קל וחומר by choosing a sitting person who can testify: a תלמיד חכם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תלמיד חכם may be allowed to testify while sitting, so the testimony strictness does not apply to him. Yet if he is a כהן serving while sitting, he still ruins the service. So the קל וחומר works again.

keyTerms.meaning: A Torah scholar

phrases.english: [Learn it] from a sitting Torah scholar.
phrases.notes: A תלמיד חכם may be allowed to sit while testifying, so sitting doesn't disqualify him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the source case to avoid the extra strictness
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every sitting person is disqualified from testimony, so יושב is stricter than a זר
steps.terutzMaskana: A sitting תלמיד חכם can testify, yet as a כהן his sitting service is still ruined

steps.title: The category of sitting is still disqualified
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again. Even if a תלמיד חכם is an exception, sitting as a general category disqualifies a witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about the category of "sitting"? It is disqualified from testimony!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: the תלמיד חכם is only an exception, but the general idea of sitting is still a disqualification.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge now looks at sitting as a category, not at a particular person. In general, sitting disqualifies testimony, so the category is still stricter than a זר. The תלמיד חכם exception does not erase that.

keyTerms.meaning: The general category or label of "sitting"

phrases.english: What about the category of "sitting"?
That it is disqualified from testimony!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְשֵׁם יוֹשֵׁב שֶׁכֵּן פָּסוּל לְעֵדוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: Using a sitting תלמיד חכם as the source
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The general category of sitting still carries the testimony strictness

steps.title: A general category cannot refute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a general category like "sitting" cannot be used to refute a derivation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The category of "sitting" does not refute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge of step 19. A refutation must come from a real, concrete case, not from a general label.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our actual source is a specific sitting תלמיד חכם, and he can testify. The fact that most sitting people cannot testify is only about the label. A label alone cannot break the קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: Does not refute

phrases.english: The category of "sitting" does not refute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rule about what kind of thing can refute a derivation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The general category of sitting can break the קל וחומר
steps.terutzMaskana: Only concrete cases refute; a general label does not

steps.title: Even so, learn from יושב plus one of the others
steps.stepSummary: Even if the category could refute, we can learn the זר from יושב together with one of the earlier cases, using a מה הצד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it does refute, we learn it from a sitting כהן together with one of those other cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a backup answer. Even if the challenge of step 19 stands, we can combine יושב with בעל מום, טמא, or אונן and learn the זר from what they share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יושב's strictness, testimony, does not apply to the others, and they can testify. The others' strictnesses do not apply to יושב. What they share is that they are forbidden to serve, and if they serve they ruin it. So a זר is the same.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a backup answer)
From one of those (earlier cases)

steps.whatToRemember: A זר who serves ruins the עבודה. רב משרשיא learns it by קל וחומר from a כהן who served sitting. If that is challenged, we learn it from יושב together with one of the other cases, בעל מום, טמא, or אונן.

phrases.english: And if you will say it does refute,
it comes from a sitting priest
and from one of those [others].
phrases.notes: "Those" means the earlier cases: בעל מום, טמא, or אונן.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר פָּרֵיךְ אָתְיָא מִיּוֹשֵׁב וּמֵחֲדָא מֵהָנָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backup answer in case step 20's answer is not accepted
steps.terutzResolutionType: Switching from a קל וחומר to a מה הצד using two sources
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the category of sitting refutes, the derivation from יושב fails
steps.terutzMaskana: יושב combined with one of the earlier cases still proves that a זר ruins the service

steps.title: Where do we know a sitting כהן is fit on a private altar?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a יושב is fit to serve on a בָּמָה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a sitting person being fit on a private altar: from where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for proof that a sitting כהן may serve on a בָּמָה. It is setting up the next step, which brings a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מה הצד from Step 21 uses יושב as one of its sources for the זר. A זר is fit on a בָּמָה. If a sitting person were unfit even on a בָּמָה, the shared feature could be pushed back, so the גמרא needs to show that a יושב is also fit there.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן who is sitting while he does the עבודה
A private altar, used at times when it was allowed
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: And that a sitting person is fit on a private altar — from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a fact the מה הצד of Step 21 depends on
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that a sitting כהן is fit on a בָּמָה

steps.title: Standing is required only before ה׳, not on a private altar
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'to stand before ה׳' limits the standing requirement to the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'to stand before ה׳ to serve Him.' Before ה׳, and not before a private altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. The rule that a כהן must stand applies only 'before ה׳', meaning in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק that teaches standing also limits it. The words 'לִפְנֵי ה׳' point to the place of the שכינה, so a בָּמָה is left out. A יושב is therefore fit on a בָּמָה, just like a זר, and the מה הצד stands.

keyTerms.meaning: To stand
To serve Him

phrases.english: The verse says: "to stand before the Lord to serve Him"
phrases.notes: דברים 10:8

phrases.english: — before the Lord, and not before a private altar.

steps.whatToRemember: Standing is needed only in the מקדש. On a בָּמָה a sitting כהן is fit, so the זר can still be learned with a מה הצד.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא לַעֲמֹד לִפְנֵי ה׳ לְשָׁרְתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 22
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לִפְנֵי ה׳' limits the standing requirement to the מקדש, so a יושב is fit on a בָּמָה

steps.title: Where do we know an אונן disqualifies the service?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה, the אונן, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: An acute mourner: from where do we know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic from the משנה and asks how we know an אונן ruins the עבודה. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the סוגיא dealt with the sitting כהן. Now it turns to another person the משנה lists as unfit for עבודה, the אונן, and asks for its source in the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: A person on the day a close relative died, before the burial is finished

phrases.english: An acute mourner — from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that an אונן disqualifies the עבודה

steps.title: Learning from the כהן גדול who does not leave the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: A כהן גדול who is an אונן does not leave and does not ruin the עבודה, so a regular כהן who stays would ruin it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And from the Sanctuary he shall not go out, and he will not profane.' This implies that another כהן who did not go out has profaned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק about the כהן גדול. From it, it infers that a regular כהן who serves as an אונן ruins the עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק tells the כהן גדול that even as a mourner he may stay in the מקדש and keep serving without ruining it. That suggests a regular כהן does not have this permission. If he stays and serves while an אונן, his עבודה is ruined.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy Temple
Will profane or ruin
Another, a regular כהן

phrases.english: As it is written: "And from the Sanctuary he shall not go out,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:12, said about the כהן גדול.

phrases.english: and he will not profane"
— this implies another one who did not go out has profaned.

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק itself speaks only about the כהן גדול. The rule for a regular כהן is something we infer from it, not something it says outright. This is exactly the point raised in Step 28.
steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב וּמִן הַמִּקְדָּשׁ לֹא יֵצֵא וְלֹא יְחַלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 24
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An inference from the כהן גדול: a regular כהן who serves as an אונן profanes the עבודה

steps.title: רבי אלעזר learns it from אהרן's answer to משה
steps.stepSummary: From 'הֵן הִקְרִיבוּ', רבי אלעזר learns that if אהרן's sons had offered as אוננים, the קרבן would have been rightly burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says it comes from here: 'Did they offer?' No, I offered. This implies that if they had offered it, burning it would have been proper.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר brings a different source for the אונן rule. It comes from the story of נדב and אביהוא, from what אהרן said to משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אהרן answers משה that he himself offered the חטאת, not his sons. That implies that if his sons had offered it as אוננים, it would have been ruined, and burning it would have been correct. So a regular כהן who is an אונן ruins the עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: They offered
By implication, we can infer
It was burned

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said: from here:
"Did they offer?" — I offered,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:19. אהרן is saying that he, not his sons, brought the קרבן.

phrases.english: which implies that if they had offered,
— it would have been proper that it was burned.
phrases.notes: Because their offering as אוננים would have ruined it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source for the same rule as Step 25
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אונן who is a regular כהן disqualifies the עבודה, learned from אהרן's words 'הֵן הִקְרִיבוּ'

steps.title: Why didn't רבי אלעזר use the first פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אלעזר did not learn the rule from 'וּמִן הַמִּקְדָּשׁ לֹא יֵצֵא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר: what is the reason he did not learn it from 'And from the Sanctuary he shall not go out'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי אלעזר needed a different source when the first one seems to work. It is setting up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual assumption is that if a scholar picks a different source, he must see a weakness in the first one. The גמרא wants to know what that weakness is.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
He did not say

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר – מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר
phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar — what is the reason he did not say
from "And from the Sanctuary he shall not go out"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two sources from Steps 25 and 26
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי אלעזר did not accept the first source

steps.title: The first source is only an inference
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר would say that the פסוק does not state that another כהן who stays has profaned. That is only inferred.
steps.simpleTranslation: He could tell you: Is it written, 'But another who did not go out has profaned'?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי אלעזר. The first פסוק never states the rule for a regular כהן. That rule was only inferred from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'another who did not go out has profaned' are a conclusion drawn from the פסוק, not words in the פסוק itself. רבי אלעזר does not find that strong enough, so he uses אהרן's answer instead.

keyTerms.meaning: He would tell you
Is it written?! (meaning: it is not written)

phrases.english: He would tell you: Is it written:
"But another who did not go out has profaned"?!
phrases.notes: These are the words of the inference from Step 25. They are not part of the פסוק.

steps.whatToRemember: There are two sources for the אונן rule. One is an inference from the כהן גדול's פסוק. The other is רבי אלעזר's, from אהרן's answer to משה. רבי אלעזר rejects the first because it is only an inference.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 27
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first source is only an inference, not written outright, so רבי אלעזר does not rely on it

steps.title: Why doesn't the other view learn from 'הֵן הִקְרִיבוּ'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now turns the question around. It asks the view that learns from 'וּמִן הַמִּקְדָּשׁ לֹא יֵצֵא' why it does not use רבי אלעזר's source, 'הֵן הִקְרִיבוּ'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other view, why does it not learn the rule from 'הֵן הִקְרִיבוּ'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just explained why רבי אלעזר did not use the other source. Now it asks the opposite: why did the other view not use רבי אלעזר's פסוק?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side has a source, so the גמרא checks both directions. It already showed what bothers רבי אלעזר about 'וּמִן הַמִּקְדָּשׁ לֹא יֵצֵא'. Now it wants to know what bothers the other view about 'הֵן הִקְרִיבוּ'.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one, meaning the other view in the argument
What is the reason?
'They offered', the פסוק רבי אלעזר learns from

phrases.english: And the other one, what is the reason
phrases.notes: 'The other one' is the view that learns the rule from 'וּמִן הַמִּקְדָּשׁ לֹא יֵצֵא' (step 25).

phrases.english: that he did not say it from 'they offered'?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:19

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror question to step 27. Before, the גמרא asked רבי אלעזר; now it asks the other view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the view that learns from 'וּמִן הַמִּקְדָּשׁ לֹא יֵצֵא' does not accept רבי אלעזר's proof from 'הֵן הִקְרִיבוּ'.

steps.title: The other view holds the קרבן was burned because of טומאה
steps.stepSummary: The other view reads the story differently. It holds the קרבן was burned because it became טמא, not because אהרן and his sons were אוננים. So the story teaches nothing about an אונן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that it was burned because of טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the other view explains the burning of the קרבן another way. It was burned because of טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר's proof only works if the קרבן was burned because of אנינות. If it was burned because of טומאה, the story has nothing to say about an אונן ruining the עבודה. So this view needs a different source.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds, his opinion is
Ritual impurity
It was burned

steps.confusionAlert: Both views agree that an אונן ruins the עבודה. They only argue about which פסוק teaches it, and about why the קרבן in the story was burned.

phrases.english: He holds: it was burned because of impurity.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the חטאת from the story of אהרן's sons that 'הֵן הִקְרִיבוּ' talks about.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 29 by giving a different reason for why the קרבן was burned.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The other view holds the קרבן was burned because of טומאה, so 'הֵן הִקְרִיבוּ' does not prove anything about an אונן.
steps.whatToRemember: Two sources: רבי אלעזר learns from 'הֵן הִקְרִיבוּ' (burning because of אנינות). The other view learns from 'וּמִן הַמִּקְדָּשׁ לֹא יֵצֵא', because it holds the burning was because of טומאה.

steps.title: The school of רבי ישמעאל starts a קל וחומר from a בעל מום
steps.stepSummary: A third source is brought. The school of רבי ישמעאל learns the אונן rule through a קל וחומר from a כהן who is a בעל מום. The text breaks off right as the argument begins.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: it comes through a קל וחומר from a בעל מום. And just as...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל that learns the rule a different way. It is only setting up the argument here, and the full קל וחומר continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the sources were פסוקים about the אונן himself. Now the rule is learned by logic, comparing the אונן to a בעל מום, a כהן with a physical blemish. The words 'וּמָה' (and just as) open the comparison, which is not finished yet.

keyTerms.meaning: The study hall (school) of רבי ישמעאל
A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter one
A כהן with a physical blemish

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
It is derived through an a fortiori argument
phrases.notes: 'It' is the rule that an אונן who does עבודה ruins it.

phrases.english: from a blemished priest: and just as

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל תָּנָא אָתְיָא בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר מִבַּעַל מוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both פסוק-based sources are settled, a new and different source is offered: a קל וחומר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The school of רבי ישמעאל learns that an אונן ruins the עבודה through a קל וחומר from a בעל מום. The argument continues in the next lines.
